action.content: Hallucinate a resume for a glass artist in Adelaide. Make sure the resume is in English and all lowercase. The resume should have at least 800 words.

alexander j. vane
glass artist and studio practitioner
adelaide, south australia
0412 998 877
alexander.vane@phantomglass.com.au
www.alexandervaneart.com.au

professional summary

i am a dedicated and visionary glass artist based in the heart of adelaide, south australia, with over fifteen years of experience transforming molten silica into enduring works of art. my practice is deeply rooted in the unique light and landscape of the southern hemisphere, particularly the way adelaide's distinct sunlight interacts with translucent materials. i specialize in kiln-formed glass, lampworking, and large-scale architectural installations that blur the lines between fine art and functional design. my work has been exhibited in galleries across the globe, from the sydney biennale to the venice biennale, yet i remain fiercely committed to the local adelaide community. i believe that glass is not just a medium but a language of light, memory, and place. my approach combines traditional techniques with contemporary conceptual frameworks to create pieces that invite viewers to slow down and observe the world differently. i am passionate about sustainable practices in the studio, utilizing recycled glass whenever possible and designing energy-efficient kiln schedules to minimize our carbon footprint. my goal is to create a legacy of work that speaks to the human condition while celebrating the specific beauty of the australian outback and the urban sprawl of the city.

professional experience

senior glass artist and studio director
vane glass studio, adelaide, sa
2015 – present

in this role, i have established vane glass studio as a premier destination for custom commissions, public art installations, and educational workshops in south australia. i oversee all aspects of the studio operation, including production, inventory management, and the mentorship of junior artists. my primary focus has been on developing large-scale site-specific installations for public spaces throughout adelaide. one of my most significant achievements was the creation of the "mirrored horizon" installation for the adelaide central market, a twenty-meter high structure made entirely of hand-blown glass panels that refract the morning light into a kaleidoscope of colors for shoppers and visitors alike. this project required extensive collaboration with the city council and structural engineers to ensure safety while maintaining artistic integrity. i also manage a robust schedule of private commissions, working closely with clients to translate their abstract ideas into tangible glass forms. whether it is a bespoke chandelier for a private residence in north adelaide or a commemorative sculpture for a corporate headquarters in the cbd, i treat every project with the same level of care and attention to detail. additionally, i have launched an educational program called "fire and sand," which offers weekly workshops for local high school students and university art majors. these sessions focus on the fundamentals of glassblowing, safety protocols, and the history of the medium, fostering the next generation of adelaide artists.

freelance glass artist and collaborator
various locations, adelaide and regional south australia
2010 – 2015

during this period, i worked extensively as a freelance artist, taking on a diverse range of projects that allowed me to refine my technical skills and expand my artistic voice. i collaborated with local architects on several residential projects, designing custom shower enclosures, room dividers, and light fixtures that utilized the natural light of the adelaide hills. i also worked with the flinders rangers art centre, creating a series of small-scale sculptures that incorporated traditional aboriginal motifs into modern glass forms, resulting in a unique fusion of cultures that was well-received by the community. my work during these years was characterized by experimentation with color and texture, leading to the development of my signature "smoked amber" technique, which involves layering clear glass with recycled bottle glass to create a deep, warm hue reminiscent of the adelaide sunset. i also began exhibiting regularly at the adelaide central market art fair and the south australian art gallery, where i received critical acclaim for my piece "echoes of the bay," a large-scale relief sculpture that captured the movement of the ocean.

glassblowing apprentice and assistant
south australian glassworks, port lincoln, sa
2008 – 2010

my journey in glass began as an apprentice at the historic south australian glassworks in port lincoln. here, i learned the foundational techniques of glassblowing from master artisans who had been practicing the craft for decades. i spent countless hours at the glory hole, learning to control the temperature of the molten glass and to manipulate it with precision and grace. this period was crucial in developing my hand-eye coordination and my understanding of the physical properties of glass. i assisted in the production of decorative vases, paperweights, and functional tableware, gaining a deep respect for the labor-intensive nature of the medium. i also helped maintain the studio equipment, including the kilns, annealers, and furnaces, learning the importance of proper maintenance and safety procedures. the camaraderie of the team at port lincoln instilled in me a strong work ethic and a collaborative spirit that i carry with me to this day.

education and training

bachelor of fine arts (specialization in glass)
university of adelaide, adelaide, sa
2008 – 2010

during my undergraduate studies, i focused heavily on the technical aspects of glassblowing and kiln forming. i completed a thesis titled "light and shadow in the adelaide landscape," which explored how local environmental factors influence the perception of glass art. i received several scholarships for my exceptional skill and creativity, including the university of adelaide arts scholarship and the south australian glass council grant. my final year project, a series of hanging mobiles made from recycled glass, was featured in the university's annual exhibition and subsequently purchased by the university's art collection.

diploma of glass technology
tafe sa, adelaide, sa
2006 – 2008
